title: Quantization profiles impact on function-call JSON schema adherence (FP8 / INT8) - validation & calibration workflow
creator: Ethan Zhao
description: Background: We have observed intermittent failures in structured output / function calling when serving quantized variants (FP8 and INT8). Failures range from minor schema drift (missing optional keys, string/number type flips) to outright invalid JSON that breaks downstream tooling. Hypothesis: quantization-induced tokenization differences and low-precision softmax logits cause different decoding paths (truncated strings, dropped delimiters) under beam/greedy decoding. This ticket defines a calibration + validation workflow and implements deterministic json-schema adherence tests to measure and mitigate regression across quant profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Create a reproducible calibration workflow for FP8 and INT8 profiles that produces calibration artifacts and configuration metadata.
Integrate an automated JSON schema adherence test in CI that runs on nightly quantized model builds for core function-calling endpoints.
Achieve >=95% pass rate on the function-calling JSON schema suite across the official calibration dataset for both FP8 and INT8; investigate and triage remaining fails.
Document mitigation strategies (prompt-level anchors, tokenization-safe canonicalizers, constrained decoding parameters) and ship at least one runtime guard (schema-aware fallback) in runtime-1.24.
Performance regressions compared to float baseline: latency increase <=5% p50, and token-cost delta documented in release notes.
test_plan: Build a canonical JSON schema test harness that accepts: schema file (json-schema v7), prompt template, canonical function spec, expected outputs (golden examples).
Run decoded outputs through strict jsonschema validation and collect failure categories: missing_required, type_mismatch, enum_mismatch, truncated_json, extra_fields.
Compute metrics: schema_pass_rate, per-category counts, sample-level edit-distance to golden JSON, and token-level divergence score (KL over token distributions).

Execute tests across float32 baseline, FP8 profile A/B (e4m3/e5m2 variants), and INT8 symmetric/asymmetric profiles with at least 500 diversified prompts covering nested objects, arrays, enums, and numeric edge-cases.
Add CI job that uploads test artifacts to internal eval dashboard and attaches failing examples to the Linear ticket automatically.
Include regression thresholds that block release if schema_pass_rate falls below 90% for critical function-calls.
steps: 1) Dataset: assemble a calibration+validation set of 1k prompts derived from production function-call traces (anonymized) + synthetic edge cases. See PM dataset spec: drive.redwood.com/datasets/quant-funcs-2026.
2) Calibration infra: reuse ENG-8120 histogram collection and extend to record per-layer activation min/max and outlier stats during warmup runs.
3) Profile generation: produce FP8 and INT8 quant profiles with per-channel calibration and optional bias-correction; store as artifacts with SHA256 and metadata file.
4) Model builds: produce quantized builds for each profile targeting runtime-1.24; tag builds with profile name and dataset used for calibration.
5) Run structured-output tests: invoke function-calling API endpoints with deterministic decoding (seeded) and stricter decoding params (no sampling) to isolate numeric precision effects.

6) Failure triage: classify failures and try targeted mitigations: increase decode temperature->0, force eos penalties, tokenization escaping for JSON delimiters, and post-decode canonicalizer with best-effort repair.
7) If repair succeeds consistently, implement runtime schema-aware fallback: on schema fail, re-decode with float fallback model or constrained decoding policy.
8) Document results, update release notes, and run a short canary in dedicated to validate in traffic-like conditions.

decisions: Use json-schema v7 validator as the canonical pass/fail gate in CI (consistent across infra).
Adopt two-tier mitigation: 1) best-effort canonicalizer on decode, 2) runtime fallback to float variant for a single retry on schema failure.
Prioritize FP8-e4m3 and INT8-asymmetric profiles for initial release; defer aggressive asymmetric INT8 quant recipes until additional calibration heuristics are validated.
Require calibration artifact provenance (dataset id, seed, layer stats) be stored with release artifact for auditability.
